simple: the small computer board that keeps a drone stable and follows commands.
analogy: the waiter's brain with its senses and nerves (a proposed F10 mapping, see NOTES).
precise: an embedded board that combines a microcontroller running a real-time operating system and a flight stack, inertial and other sensors, interfaces to radios, GNSS, ESCs and payloads, logging storage and power input; "autopilot" is the name the Pixhawk standards and flight-stack documents use for this unit.
source: D1 of F10-07 (Pixhawk Special Interest Group, coordinated by the Dronecode Foundation, "Pixhawk Standards" (tier 1): DS-009 (connector standard), DS-010 (autopilot bus), DS-011, DS-012, DS-016, DS-018, DS-020 (autopilot standards), DS-014 (payload bus), DS-017 (radio interface), DS-019 (versions)); D2 of F10-07 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): flight controller hardware, sensors and redundancy, architecture overview (modules, work queues, uORB), outputs, logging) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: shared rule books that say how a flight controller's connectors and modules should look, so parts from different makers fit together.
analogy: every tray in the hall having handles in the same place, so any waiter can pick up any tray.
precise: open hardware standards published by the Pixhawk Special Interest Group (coordinated by the Dronecode Foundation), including a connector standard (DS-009), an autopilot bus standard (DS-010), several autopilot standards (DS-011, DS-012, DS-016, DS-018, DS-020), a payload bus (DS-014), a radio interface (DS-017) and a versions document (DS-019).
source: D1 of F10-07 (Pixhawk Special Interest Group, coordinated by the Dronecode Foundation, "Pixhawk Standards" (tier 1): DS-009 (connector standard), DS-010 (autopilot bus), DS-011, DS-012, DS-016, DS-018, DS-020 (autopilot standards), DS-014 (payload bus), DS-017 (radio interface), DS-019 (versions)); C1 of F10-07 (University Authoring Guide (repository file UNIVERSITY_AUTHORING_GUIDE.html), section 4.8 (F10 source registry: Pixhawk standards list, PX4 on NuttX, ArduPilot porting note) and section 5.15 (DN202 course card) — opened in this build; a map to sources, not a source for technical claims) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the big program on the flight controller: drivers, estimator, controllers, logging and communication.
analogy: all the habits the waiter's brain uses while carrying.
precise: the firmware above the operating system that implements sensor drivers, state estimation, control, mixing, outputs, failsafes, logging and the ground-station link; PX4 (on NuttX) and ArduPilot (on ChibiOS, on STM32-based boards in its porting guide) are the two open flight stacks studied in this university.
source: D2 of F10-07 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): flight controller hardware, sensors and redundancy, architecture overview (modules, work queues, uORB), outputs, logging); D3 of F10-07 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): autopilot hardware, the vehicle code's scheduler, porting to a new flight controller board (STM32 boards using ChibiOS, as the guide's registry records)); C1 of F10-07 (University Authoring Guide (repository file UNIVERSITY_AUTHORING_GUIDE.html), section 4.8 (F10 source registry: Pixhawk standards list, PX4 on NuttX, ArduPilot porting note) and section 5.15 (DN202 course card) — opened in this build; a map to sources, not a source for technical claims) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the fastest control loop, which keeps the drone's turning speeds where they should be.
analogy: the quick wrist corrections that stop the tray tipping.
precise: the innermost loop of the cascaded controller (F10-16): it compares estimated body rates with rate setpoints and outputs torque commands to the mixer, once per control period.
source: D2 of F10-07 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): flight controller hardware, sensors and redundancy, architecture overview (modules, work queues, uORB), outputs, logging); D3 of F10-07 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): autopilot hardware, the vehicle code's scheduler, porting to a new flight controller board (STM32 boards using ChibiOS, as the guide's registry records)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a labelled socket on the board for one kind of device.
analogy: the tray's handles, each shaped for one hand.
precise: a connector that carries one interface (UART, I2C, CAN, PWM or other output, RC input, power and sense lines) with defined pins, signal levels and supply; types and pinouts are set by the board's documentation and, for compliant boards, by the Pixhawk connector standard.
source: D1 of F10-07 (Pixhawk Special Interest Group, coordinated by the Dronecode Foundation, "Pixhawk Standards" (tier 1): DS-009 (connector standard), DS-010 (autopilot bus), DS-011, DS-012, DS-016, DS-018, DS-020 (autopilot standards), DS-014 (payload bus), DS-017 (radio interface), DS-019 (versions)); D5 of F10-07 (The documentation of the flight controller chosen for the course kit (tier 1, dossier part F): processor, sensors and buses, ports, connector pinouts, signal levels, supply ranges, standard compliance) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the program on a computer or tablet that shows what the drone is doing and changes its settings.
analogy: the head waiter's desk where the plan for the evening is written.
precise: software that talks to the flight stack over USB or a telemetry radio, usually with MAVLink (F10-12), to display state, set parameters, calibrate sensors, test motors and plan missions.
source: D2 of F10-07 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): flight controller hardware, sensors and redundancy, architecture overview (modules, work queues, uORB), outputs, logging); D3 of F10-07 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): autopilot hardware, the vehicle code's scheduler, porting to a new flight controller board (STM32 boards using ChibiOS, as the guide's registry records)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a moment when the loop should have run but did not.
analogy: the waiter looking away from the tray for a moment.
precise: a periodic job that has not finished (or here, not started) by its next release; the control law then acts on older data or not at all for that period.
source: D4 of F10-07 (Jane W. S. Liu, "Real-Time Systems", and Giorgio Buttazzo, "Hard Real-Time Computing Systems" (tier 3, guide registry 4.7): fixed-priority scheduling, response-time analysis, blocking by non-preemptible sections and resources); R2 of F10-07 (R2 — lab run of Listing 2 with fcsim.hpp (sched_sim.log), same toolchain, exit code 0; Figure 2 drawn from the same simulator) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how late a task starts compared with when it should start.
analogy: a correction that comes a little late, so the tray tips a bit further first.
precise: the variation of the delay between a periodic task's release time and the time it first runs; measured from timestamps, reported as a histogram or maximum.
source: D4 of F10-07 (Jane W. S. Liu, "Real-Time Systems", and Giorgio Buttazzo, "Hard Real-Time Computing Systems" (tier 3, guide registry 4.7): fixed-priority scheduling, response-time analysis, blocking by non-preemptible sections and resources) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a sensor that measures air pressure; pressure drops as you go up.
analogy: the waiter's ears popping in the lift (a proposed F10 mapping, see NOTES).
precise: a sensor that measures static air pressure (and usually its own temperature); a flight controller converts the pressure change since a reference into a height change with a model of the atmosphere.
source: D1 of F10-08 (Randal W. Beard, Timothy W. McLain, "Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice" (tier 3): the chapter on sensors (accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors and altitude, digital compass and declination, GPS), with the hydrostatic and ideal-gas relations) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how high you are, worked out from how much the pressure has dropped.
analogy: counting floors by how much your ears popped.
precise: the height above a reference pressure p0 computed from the hydrostatic equation; with constant temperature T, h = (R·T / (M·g))·ln(p0/p); it changes when the weather changes p0.
source: D1 of F10-08 (Randal W. Beard, Timothy W. McLain, "Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice" (tier 3): the chapter on sensors (accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors and altitude, digital compass and declination, GPS), with the hydrostatic and ideal-gas relations); D6 of F10-08 ("U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976" (NOAA, NASA, US Air Force) and the CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants (NIST) (tier 1): atmospheric model, gas constant, molar mass of air, standard gravity) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a constant magnetic field from the drone's own parts that adds to the Earth's field in every reading.
analogy: a lamp on the terrace that is always on your left, so you mistake its glow for the sunset.
precise: a field vector fixed in the body frame (from magnetised parts and steady currents) that shifts every magnetometer reading by the same vector; it moves the centre of the sphere traced by readings in all orientations away from the origin.
source: D1 of F10-08 (Randal W. Beard, Timothy W. McLain, "Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice" (tier 3): the chapter on sensors (accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors and altitude, digital compass and declination, GPS), with the hydrostatic and ideal-gas relations); D2 of F10-08 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): sensor orientation and calibration (gyroscope, accelerometer, level, magnetometer, temperature), compass interference and selection, barometer and GNSS setup, estimator delays) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: metal near the sensor that bends the Earth's field, differently in each direction.
analogy: a curved window that bends the sunset's light.
precise: distortion by magnetically soft material that is induced by the external field and depends on orientation; it turns the sphere of readings into an ellipsoid, corrected by a 3×3 matrix.
source: D1 of F10-08 (Randal W. Beard, Timothy W. McLain, "Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice" (tier 3): the chapter on sensors (accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors and altitude, digital compass and declination, GPS), with the hydrostatic and ideal-gas relations) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the compass direction worked out correctly even when the drone is tilted.
analogy: knowing which way you face even while leaning to put down a glass.
precise: the heading obtained after rotating the body-frame magnetic field into the horizontal plane using roll and pitch from the attitude estimate, then taking atan2 of the horizontal components.
source: D1 of F10-08 (Randal W. Beard, Timothy W. McLain, "Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice" (tier 3): the chapter on sensors (accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors and altitude, digital compass and declination, GPS), with the hydrostatic and ideal-gas relations) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the angle between where a compass points and true north.
analogy: the sunset is not exactly in the west; how far off depends on where you are.
precise: the angle between magnetic north and true north at a location; it varies with place and slowly with time, and must be added to a magnetic heading to get a true heading.
source: D1 of F10-08 (Randal W. Beard, Timothy W. McLain, "Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice" (tier 3): the chapter on sensors (accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors and altitude, digital compass and declination, GPS), with the hydrostatic and ideal-gas relations) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: satellites that let a receiver work out where it is on Earth.
analogy: finding your place in the crowd by hearing several friends call from known tables (a proposed F10 mapping).
precise: a system of satellites broadcasting timing signals; a receiver measures ranges to several satellites and solves for its position, velocity and clock offset; GPS is one such system.
source: D1 of F10-08 (Randal W. Beard, Timothy W. McLain, "Small Unmanned Aircraft: Theory and Practice" (tier 3): the chapter on sensors (accelerometers, rate gyros, pressure sensors and altitude, digital compass and declination, GPS), with the hydrostatic and ideal-gas relations); D5 of F10-08 (Pratap Misra, Per Enge, "Global Positioning System: Signals, Measurements, and Performance" (tier 3): ranging, the navigation solution, error sources, multipath, dilution of precision, differential and carrier-phase methods) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

term: Fix (GNSS fix) and its accuracy estimate
simple: one position answer from the receiver, with its own guess of how good it is.
analogy: "I think I am near the window table, give or take two tables".
precise: a navigation solution reported by the receiver with a fix type (no fix, 2D, 3D and others the receiver documents), the number of satellites used and accuracy estimates; the estimator uses these to decide how much to trust the fix.
source: D2 of F10-08 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): sensor orientation and calibration (gyroscope, accelerometer, level, magnetometer, temperature), compass interference and selection, barometer and GNSS setup, estimator delays); D4 of F10-08 (The datasheets of the IMU, barometer, magnetometer and GNSS module chosen for the course kit, and the GNSS receiver's protocol documentation (tier 1, dossier part F)); D5 of F10-08 (Pratap Misra, Per Enge, "Global Positioning System: Signals, Measurements, and Performance" (tier 3): ranging, the navigation solution, error sources, multipath, dilution of precision, differential and carrier-phase methods) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: telling the software which way the board or sensor is turned on the drone.
analogy: knowing whether you hold the tray with your left or right hand.
precise: a fixed rotation between a sensor's own axes and the vehicle's body axes, set in the flight stack's configuration; a wrong value makes every correction go the wrong way.
source: D2 of F10-08 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): sensor orientation and calibration (gyroscope, accelerometer, level, magnetometer, temperature), compass interference and selection, barometer and GNSS setup, estimator delays); D3 of F10-08 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): sensor and compass calibration, compass-motor interference compensation, barometer, GNSS) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a soft layer between the frame and the flight controller that soaks up fast shaking.
analogy: the folded cloth under the glasses (a proposed F10 mapping, see NOTES).
precise: a compliant, damped support that, together with the mass it carries, forms a mass–spring–damper; above about √2 times its natural frequency it transmits less vibration than a rigid mount, below that it transmits as much or more.
source: D1 of F10-09 (Singiresu S. Rao, "Mechanical Vibrations" (tier 3): single-degree-of-freedom systems, natural frequency, damping ratio, base excitation and transmissibility, vibration isolation, multi-degree-of-freedom mounts); R1 of F10-09 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F10-09/isolator.log), toolchain g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the frequency at which the board likes to bounce on its mount.
analogy: the rate at which the glasses sway on a soft cloth if you nudge the tray once.
precise: fn = (1/2π)·√(k/m) for stiffness k and supported mass m; excitation near fn is amplified.
source: D1 of F10-09 (Singiresu S. Rao, "Mechanical Vibrations" (tier 3): single-degree-of-freedom systems, natural frequency, damping ratio, base excitation and transmissibility, vibration isolation, multi-degree-of-freedom mounts) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much of the frame's shaking reaches the board, as a ratio.
analogy: how much of the deck's hum still ripples the drinks.
precise: for base excitation of a mass–spring–damper, the ratio of the mass's amplitude to the base's amplitude, T(r) = √(1 + (2ζr)²) / √((1 − r²)² + (2ζr)²), with r = f/fn.
source: D1 of F10-09 (Singiresu S. Rao, "Mechanical Vibrations" (tier 3): single-degree-of-freedom systems, natural frequency, damping ratio, base excitation and transmissibility, vibration isolation, multi-degree-of-freedom mounts); R1 of F10-09 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F10-09/isolator.log), toolchain g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: when the shaking is bigger than the sensor can measure, so its readings stick at the largest number.
analogy: a glass that jumps off the tray: the cloth cannot fix that.
precise: the sensor's output is limited to its full-scale range; samples beyond it are replaced by the limit value, which distorts the signal and, for asymmetric peaks, shifts its mean.
source: D5 of F10-09 (The datasheet of the IMU on the course's flight controller (tier 1, dossier part F): full-scale ranges, internal sampling and output rates, digital filters, mechanical resonance and vibration sensitivity); R2 of F10-09 (R2 — lab run of Listing 2 (clipping.log), same toolchain, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one number per axis that says how strongly the sensor is shaking.
analogy: how big the ripples on the drinks are.
precise: in this chapter, the standard deviation of an accelerometer axis over a window (the vibration's RMS with the mean removed); PX4 and ArduPilot log their own vibration metrics and clipping counters, defined in their documentation.
source: D2 of F10-09 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): vibration isolation, log analysis of vibration and accelerometer clipping, IMU filtering and notch filters, mounting the flight controller); D3 of F10-09 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): measuring vibration, vibration damping, clipping, harmonic notch filters) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many times per second a propeller blade passes the same place.
analogy: the beat of the ship's engine felt through the deck.
precise: the rotation frequency multiplied by the number of blades; aerodynamic and structural excitation of a multirotor's frame appears at the rotation frequency (imbalance), the blade-pass frequency and their harmonics.
source: D1 of F10-09 (Singiresu S. Rao, "Mechanical Vibrations" (tier 3): single-degree-of-freedom systems, natural frequency, damping ratio, base excitation and transmissibility, vibration isolation, multi-degree-of-freedom mounts); D2 of F10-09 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): vibration isolation, log analysis of vibration and accelerometer clipping, IMU filtering and notch filters, mounting the flight controller) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the agreed code in which the flight controller tells an ESC how hard to drive its motor.
analogy: the nerve signal's code between brain and muscle (the registered F10 mapping "ESC = the nerve controller for each muscle").
precise: the electrical and timing format of the signal on the ESC's input: a pulse whose width encodes throttle (several variants with different pulse lengths and rates), or a digital frame of bits with a value and a checksum; the flight stack's output driver and the ESC must be set to the same protocol.
source: D1 of F10-10 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): ESCs and motors, output protocols (PWM, OneShot, DShot, bidirectional DShot), ESC calibration, motor test, output groups, CAN ESCs, motor-speed notch filtering); D2 of F10-10 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): ESCs and motor protocols, ESC calibration, motor test, ESC telemetry, harmonic notch with ESC speed) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a repeating pulse whose length means "how much throttle".
analogy: squeezing a hand for a longer or shorter time to say "more" or "less".
precise: a pulse repeated at a frame rate, whose high time between two end points maps linearly to zero and full throttle; it is the same kind of signal as a hobby servo's command (F1-69), and the ESC must know or learn the end points.
source: D1 of F10-10 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): ESCs and motors, output protocols (PWM, OneShot, DShot, bidirectional DShot), ESC calibration, motor test, output groups, CAN ESCs, motor-speed notch filtering); D2 of F10-10 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): ESCs and motor protocols, ESC calibration, motor test, ESC telemetry, harmonic notch with ESC speed) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: teaching an ESC which pulse lengths mean "stop" and "full".
analogy: agreeing with a friend how long a squeeze means "stop" and how long means "go".
precise: a procedure in which the ESC records the pulse widths it receives as its zero and full-throttle end points; ESCs on one vehicle must be calibrated to the same end points as the controller's output range.
source: D1 of F10-10 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): ESCs and motors, output protocols (PWM, OneShot, DShot, bidirectional DShot), ESC calibration, motor test, output groups, CAN ESCs, motor-speed notch filtering); D2 of F10-10 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): ESCs and motor protocols, ESC calibration, motor test, ESC telemetry, harmonic notch with ESC speed); D3 of F10-10 (The documentation of the ESCs chosen for the course kit (tier 1, dossier part F): supported protocols, calibration, telemetry, direction setting, limits and protection) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: sending the throttle as a short binary number with a check code, instead of a pulse length.
analogy: saying a number out loud instead of squeezing longer or shorter.
precise: a protocol in which each command is a frame of bits (a throttle or command value, a telemetry-request bit and a checksum), each bit sent as a pulse of one of two widths in a fixed bit period; DShot is the family named in the PX4 and ArduPilot documentation, with a bidirectional variant in which the ESC replies on the same wire.
source: D1 of F10-10 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): ESCs and motors, output protocols (PWM, OneShot, DShot, bidirectional DShot), ESC calibration, motor test, output groups, CAN ESCs, motor-speed notch filtering); D2 of F10-10 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): ESCs and motor protocols, ESC calibration, motor test, ESC telemetry, harmonic notch with ESC speed); C1 of F10-10 (University Authoring Guide (repository file UNIVERSITY_AUTHORING_GUIDE.html), section 4.8 (registry row "ESC and motor-protocol notes (PWM, OneShot, DShot, bidirectional DShot) in the PX4 and ArduPilot documentation") — opened in this build; a map, not a source for technical claims) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a few extra bits computed from the message, so the receiver can tell if it arrived damaged.
analogy: repeating the last digit of a phone number back to check you heard it right.
precise: a short value computed from the data bits by a fixed rule (here the XOR of three 4-bit groups); the receiver recomputes it and rejects frames that do not match; it detects every single-bit error of this design but not every multi-bit error.
source: R2 of F10-10 (R2 — lab run of Listing 2 (ushot.log), same toolchain, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: information the ESC sends back, such as motor speed.
analogy: the muscle telling the brain how hard it is working.
precise: data returned by the ESC (for example electrical speed, and on some ESCs voltage, current and temperature), either on the signal wire in a bidirectional protocol or on a separate serial or CAN connection; motor-speed telemetry lets the flight stack place its vibration notch filters on the motors' frequencies.
source: D1 of F10-10 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): ESCs and motors, output protocols (PWM, OneShot, DShot, bidirectional DShot), ESC calibration, motor test, output groups, CAN ESCs, motor-speed notch filtering); D2 of F10-10 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): ESCs and motor protocols, ESC calibration, motor test, ESC telemetry, harmonic notch with ESC speed) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: spinning each motor alone, from the ground station, to check it.
analogy: wiggling each finger once to check the nerves before lifting the tray.
precise: a ground-station function that commands one output at a time at a chosen level for a short time, used with propellers removed to verify motor order, direction of rotation and response before flight.
source: D1 of F10-10 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): ESCs and motors, output protocols (PWM, OneShot, DShot, bidirectional DShot), ESC calibration, motor test, output groups, CAN ESCs, motor-speed notch filtering); D2 of F10-10 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): ESCs and motor protocols, ESC calibration, motor test, ESC telemetry, harmonic notch with ESC speed) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small board in the battery cable that feeds the flight controller and measures the battery's voltage and current.
analogy: the marks on the waiter's water bottle plus her count of glasses (a proposed F10 mapping, see NOTES).
precise: a board between the battery and the vehicle's power distribution that supplies the flight controller from a regulator and reports battery voltage and current, either as analog voltages for the controller's ADC or as digital values over a bus (I2C, SMBus or CAN).
source: D4 of F10-11 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): power modules (analog and digital), battery estimation and calibration (voltage divider, amperes per volt), load compensation, smart batteries, battery failsafe); D5 of F10-11 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): power monitors and their calibration, battery failsafe, smart batteries); D6 of F10-11 (The documentation of the power module and of the flight controller's power port chosen for the course kit (tier 1, dossier part F): sensor type, scales, limits, regulator, connector and pinout (Pixhawk connector standard DS-009 where the board complies)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two resistors that scale a big voltage down to a small one the chip can measure.
analogy: a measuring cup that holds one eleventh of the bottle, so it fits on the scale.
precise: a series pair R1, R2 with Vout = Vin·R2/(R1 + R2); the flight controller multiplies the measured pin voltage by the inverse ratio (the "divider" setting).
source: D7 of F10-11 (Paul Horowitz, Winfield Hill, "The Art of Electronics" (tier 3): voltage dividers, current sensing with shunts and amplifiers, Hall-effect sensors, ADC errors); D4 of F10-11 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): power modules (analog and digital), battery estimation and calibration (voltage divider, amperes per volt), load compensation, smart batteries, battery failsafe) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a part that turns the battery current into a small voltage.
analogy: a flow meter in the bottle's straw.
precise: a low-value shunt resistor with an amplifier, or a Hall-effect sensor, whose output voltage is offset + gain × current; the flight controller needs the gain (or its inverse, amperes per volt) and the offset.
source: D7 of F10-11 (Paul Horowitz, Winfield Hill, "The Art of Electronics" (tier 3): voltage dividers, current sensing with shunts and amplifiers, Hall-effect sensors, ADC errors); D6 of F10-11 (The documentation of the power module and of the flight controller's power port chosen for the course kit (tier 1, dossier part F): sensor type, scales, limits, regulator, connector and pinout (Pixhawk connector standard DS-009 where the board complies)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much charge has been taken from the battery since take-off.
analogy: counting the glasses of water drunk.
precise: the integral of measured current over time, in milliampere-hours (1 mAh = 3.6 coulombs); it is exact only if the current measurement is calibrated.
source: D3 of F10-11 (Thomas B. Reddy (ed.), "Linden's Handbook of Batteries" (tier 3): lithium-ion and lithium-polymer cells, capacity, internal resistance, temperature and ageing, safety hazards); D4 of F10-11 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): power modules (analog and digital), battery estimation and calibration (voltage divider, amperes per volt), load compensation, smart batteries, battery failsafe) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the battery voltage dropping while a large current is drawn, and coming back afterwards.
analogy: feeling more tired right after a sprint than you really are.
precise: the drop I·R across the pack's internal resistance R (plus wiring), so terminal voltage = open-circuit voltage − I·R; it hides the state of charge during high current. (HW302's term "Internal resistance and voltage sag", F1-71.)
source: D3 of F10-11 (Thomas B. Reddy (ed.), "Linden's Handbook of Batteries" (tier 3): lithium-ion and lithium-polymer cells, capacity, internal resistance, temperature and ageing, safety hazards) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: adding the expected drop back to the measured voltage, to judge the battery fairly during a climb.
analogy: the waiter allowing for the sprint before she judges how tired she is.
precise: estimating the open-circuit voltage as V + I·R with an estimate of R, so that battery warnings do not trigger on short high-current events.
source: D3 of F10-11 (Thomas B. Reddy (ed.), "Linden's Handbook of Batteries" (tier 3): lithium-ion and lithium-polymer cells, capacity, internal resistance, temperature and ageing, safety hazards); D4 of F10-11 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): power modules (analog and digital), battery estimation and calibration (voltage divider, amperes per volt), load compensation, smart batteries, battery failsafe) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: charging so that every cell in the pack ends up at the same level.
analogy: filling every glass on the tray to the same line.
precise: charging a series pack through its main leads while the charger monitors each cell through the balance connector and equalises cells, so that no cell is over-charged; required by LiPo packs as their makers document.
source: D1 of F10-11 (The battery maker's datasheet and safety instructions for the pack chosen for the course kit (tier 1, dossier part F): voltage window, capacity, current limits, temperature range, charging, storage, transport and disposal); D2 of F10-11 (The manual of the LiPo balance charger chosen for the course kit (tier 1): chemistries, cell counts, balance charging, storage mode, safety features) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the pilot's hand-held controller and the small radio on the drone that hears it.
analogy: the head waiter's hand signals and the waiter's eyes (a proposed F10 mapping, see NOTES).
precise: a radio pair that sends the positions of the transmitter's sticks and switches as channel values in repeated frames; the receiver passes them to the flight controller as PWM per channel, a pulse train, or a serial protocol, as its maker documents.
source: D6 of F10-12 (The documentation of the RC transmitter, RC receiver and telemetry radios chosen for the course kit (tier 1, dossier part F): protocols, binding, failsafe modes, range-check mode, RSSI and link-quality reporting, powers and approvals); D1 of F10-12 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): RC receivers and supported protocols, radio setup, telemetry radios, RC-loss and data-link-loss failsafes); D2 of F10-12 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): RC input and supported protocols, telemetry radios, radio failsafe, range checks) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one number carried by the radio link, such as the throttle stick's position.
analogy: one of the head waiter's hand signs.
precise: one value in each frame, scaled by the flight stack to a stick or switch position and mapped (channel map) to a function such as roll, pitch, throttle, yaw, flight mode or arming.
source: D1 of F10-12 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): RC receivers and supported protocols, radio setup, telemetry radios, RC-loss and data-link-loss failsafes); D2 of F10-12 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): RC input and supported protocols, telemetry radios, radio failsafe, range checks) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a two-way radio that sends the drone's status to a ground station and carries commands back.
analogy: the waiter calling back "two left on the tray".
precise: a pair of radio modems that carry a serial byte stream between a flight controller port and a ground station, usually carrying MAVLink messages; its throughput and range are much lower than a wired link.
source: D3 of F10-12 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide" (tier 2): what MAVLink is, its use between vehicles and ground stations, message signing); D1 of F10-12 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): RC receivers and supported protocols, radio setup, telemetry radios, RC-loss and data-link-loss failsafes); D2 of F10-12 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): RC input and supported protocols, telemetry radios, radio failsafe, range checks) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: what the drone does on its own when the pilot's signal stops.
analogy: "if you get lost, go back to the meeting point" (registered F10 analogy).
precise: a detection rule (no valid frame for a timeout, or a failsafe indication from the receiver) plus a configured action (for example hold, return or land); both must be configured and tested, because defaults may not suit your field.
source: D1 of F10-12 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide" (tier 2): RC receivers and supported protocols, radio setup, telemetry radios, RC-loss and data-link-loss failsafes); D2 of F10-12 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): RC input and supported protocols, telemetry radios, radio failsafe, range checks); C1 of F10-12 (University curriculum, DN202 course entry (course project, exam P) and the F10 analogy registry (failsafe, MAVLink) — opened in this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: adding up how much signal is sent, gained and lost, to see whether enough arrives.
analogy: how loudly the head waiter must call so that the waiter still hears him at the far end of the room.
precise: received power (dBm) = transmit power (dBm) + antenna gains (dBi) − cable losses (dB) − path loss (dB); the link works while received power stays above the receiver's sensitivity with a fade margin to spare.
source: D5 of F10-12 (Constantine A. Balanis, "Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design" (tier 3): Friis transmission equation, free-space path loss, antenna patterns and polarisation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much weaker a radio signal gets with distance in empty space.
analogy: a voice getting fainter across an empty hall.
precise: FSPL = 20·log10(4π·d·f/c) dB between isotropic antennas; it grows by 6.02 dB per doubling of distance and with frequency; obstacles, the ground and the vehicle body add loss on top.
source: D5 of F10-12 (Constantine A. Balanis, "Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design" (tier 3): Friis transmission equation, free-space path loss, antenna patterns and polarisation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the receiver's measure of how strong the incoming signal is.
analogy: how clearly the waiter can see the hand signals.
precise: received signal strength indicator, reported by many receivers and radios in dBm or a maker-specific scale, often alongside a link-quality figure (share of frames received); the scale and meaning come from the maker.
source: D6 of F10-12 (The documentation of the RC transmitter, RC receiver and telemetry radios chosen for the course kit (tier 1, dossier part F): protocols, binding, failsafe modes, range-check mode, RSSI and link-quality reporting, powers and approvals) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a ground test that the link still works at a distance before flying.
analogy: checking that the waiter can see the signals from every corner of the room before the shift.
precise: a test, often with the transmitter in a reduced-power mode documented by its maker, at a set distance with the vehicle turned through all headings, logging frame loss and RSSI.
source: D6 of F10-12 (The documentation of the RC transmitter, RC receiver and telemetry radios chosen for the course kit (tier 1, dossier part F): protocols, binding, failsafe modes, range-check mode, RSSI and link-quality reporting, powers and approvals); D2 of F10-12 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation" (tier 2): RC input and supported protocols, telemetry radios, radio failsafe, range checks) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
